topic: Pheasant Island: the river island that switches between Spain and France every six months

sources.title: Spanish or French? Pheasant Island is about to swap nationalities — again
The little Spanish town that found itself in France

claims.text: Spain administers Pheasant Island from 1 February to 31 July and France from 1 August to 31 January: it switches every six months.
claims.quote: It is administered by France from 1 August to 31 January. It is administered by Spain from 1 February to 31 July. (wiki); From 1 February until 31 July, Spain holds stewardship of the condominium (euronews); It switches sovereignty between France and Spain every six months, with Spain owning it from February to July and France taking over from August to January (cnn)

claims.text: It is an island in the Bidasoa river, on the border between France and Spain, between Hendaye (France) and Irun (Spain).
claims.quote: is an uninhabited river island located in the Bidasoa river, located between France and Spain (wiki); Pheasant Island is located on the Bidasoa river between Hendaye, France, and Irun, Spain (euronews)

claims.text: The island is about 200 metres long (and about 40 metres wide).
claims.quote: one of the rare occasions visitors are allowed to visit this 200-metre-long island (euronews); the island was approximately 200 metres (660 ft) long and 40 metres (130 ft) wide (wiki)

claims.text: Nobody lives on the island; it is uninhabited (population 0).
claims.quote: is an uninhabited river island (wiki); This remained the status of this uninhabited island (cnn)

claims.text: In 1659 France and Spain negotiated and signed the Treaty of the Pyrenees on the island, ending the Franco-Spanish war that began in 1635.
claims.quote: The Treaty of the Pyrenees was signed on 7 November 1659 and ended the Franco–Spanish War that had begun in 1635. Negotiations were conducted and the treaty was signed on Pheasant Island (pyr); The most important historical event to have taken place on the island was the signing of the Treaty of the Pyrenees (wiki); the Franco-Spanish War ran on from 1635 to 1659 (cnn); the patch of land in the middle of the Bidasoa River upon which the treaty was signed (cnn)

claims.text: The treaty was the climax of a series of 24 conferences between the two chief ministers.
claims.quote: This was the climax to a series of 24 conferences held between Luis Méndez de Haro

claims.text: For centuries, treaties were signed and royal brides and grooms were exchanged on the island; Louis XIV met his future wife Maria Theresa of Spain there.
claims.quote: It was for centuries a sort of “no man’s land” where international treaties were signed and royal grooms and brides were exchanged between the two kingdoms (cnn); 1659 – Louis XIV met his future wife Maria Theresa of Spain (wiki)

claims.text: Today the island is a condominium under the joint sovereignty of Spain and France, the world's smallest.
claims.quote: The island is a condominium , the world's smallest, under joint sovereignty of Spain and France (wiki); Pheasant Island, the world's smallest territory with joint custody (euronews)

claims.text: The French official responsible carries the title 'viceroy of Pheasant Island'.
claims.quote: carries the title of " viceroy of Pheasant Island", an unusual name in the French Republic

claims.text: There are no pheasants on the island.
claims.quote: There are no pheasants on the island.

claims.text: The name probably comes from a misreading: an older name meaning passage was translated into French words that ended up as 'Faisans' (pheasants).
claims.quote: The name could be a misinterpretation of some French word related to "passing" or "toll" (wiki); Then, the French translated this as Paysans, meaning peasant, before switching it to Faisans, meaning pheasant (euronews)
claims.label: probably
claims.note: Etymology is uncertain ('could be' in Wikipedia); the script says 'probably'.

claims.text: Visitors are allowed on only on rare occasions such as the handover days; access is otherwise forbidden.
claims.quote: Visitors are only allowed onto the island on very few occasions (euronews); access is forbidden, except very occasionally on heritage open days (wiki)

claims.text: The six-month alternation was set up by the 1659 treaty.
claims.quote: until 1866, when it became what is known in international law as a “condominium.”
claims.note: Rejected: CNN dates condominium status to 1866 and Wikipedia's note dates the alternation to an 1856 treaty and a 1901 agreement; the script does not date the swap.

myths.myth: The 1659 Treaty of the Pyrenees created the six-month swap.
myths.truth: Sources disagree: CNN dates condominium status to 1866; Wikipedia's note (Mermoz, International Boundaries Review) says the island became undivided by the 1856 Treaty of Bayonne and the alternation follows a 1901 agreement in force from 1902. The script avoids dating the swap.

myths.myth: The island is named after its pheasants.
myths.truth: There are no pheasants; the name is probably a mistranslation.

open_questions: Exact year the alternating administration started (1856, 1866 or 1901-1902 depending on source).
